newsitem.title: INDIA: India leftists set condition for leadership change.
newsitem.headline: India leftists set condition for leadership change.

text.p: An influential leftist bloc in India's ousted United Front coalition cautioned allies on Wednesday against naming a new candidate for the top job unless the Congress withdraws its formal claim to form a government.
The four-party communist-led Left Front said after a meeting in New Delhi that Congress president Sitaram Kesri was still his party's official candidate for the prime minister's job.

The warning, spelled out by Harkishan Singh Surjeet, general secretary of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), at a news conference, came moments after a United Front official said a new coalition government was likely to be in place by Sunday.
The Congress party triggered the fall of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government in a vote of confidence on Friday by withdrawing its support on March 30.
Kesri officially staked his claim to form a new government in a letter to President Shankar Dayal Sharma on March 31.

Although Kesri sent a letter to the United Front Convener Chandrababu Naidu on Tuesday, offering support to a new coalition leader, Surjeet said it was a half-measure because Sharma was still not informed of the party's changed stance.
"Do they (the Congress) want to determine the choice of the leader? This cannot happen," Surjeet said.
He told Reuters the Left Front would oppose naming Deve Gowda's successor at a United Front meeting on Thursday if Kesri did not first spell out his intentions to Sharma.
"There is no question of discussing the issue (of change of leadership) unless the Congress withdraws its claim," he said.

On Monday, the Congress Working Committee said it would support a new United Front government, provided the alliance named a new leader. But it did not say why it was not writing to Sharma about the move.
Earlier on Wednesday, a senior United Front leader said there was a "distinct possibility" a new government would be formed under its leadership in the next few days.
Sharma has called for a special session of parliament to meet between April 21 and 23 to allow discussion and a possible vote on the 1997/98 (April-March) budget.

A senior coalition official was asked by reporters to comment on the 1997/97 (April-March) budget, which has been called into question by left-wing parties and the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

"If a government can be formed, which is a distinct possibility, before the 20th, that budget will be handled by the new government," said the official, who asked not to be identified. "That's the hope on which we all are proceeding." Congress officials said privately they would support G.K. Moopanar, head of Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress, as Deve Gowda's successor.
The Left Front considers Moopanar, who broke away from the Congress to lead his party in the southern state of Tamil Nadu, too close to Kesri to be made prime minister.
The centre-left coalition kept its formal distance from the Congress on Wednesday.
"There is no question of a coalition with the Congress party at all. The consensus is that there should be no coalition," the United Front official said.

The United Front's decision-making Steering Committee is set to meet on Thursday at 3 p.m. (0930 GMT) to discuss a possible leadership change. Members of parliament from the 15 parties in the alliance were scheduled to endorse a new leader on Sunday.
